report.incident_summary: Conveyor 2 stopped at 2026-01-15T14:20:00 after a sequence of motor current increase, speed drop, and a controller overload trip.
report.leading_hypothesis: A mechanical obstruction (jam) caused the motor to draw excessive current, reduced conveyor speed, and triggered the drive overload protection.

timeline.observation: Motor current exceeded 12 A (12.05 A) while conveyor speed was still above the low‑speed threshold (0.684 m/s).
Conveyor speed fell below 0.6 m/s (0.596 m/s) and motor current rose further to 12.61 A.
Controller issued a drive overload trip; motor current dropped to 0 A, speed to 0 m/s, and vibration fell to idle level (0.15 mm/s).

supporting_evidence.finding: Triggered when motor current reaches or exceeds 12 A. Possible causes include mechanical obstruction or conveyor jam, excessive material load, increased belt friction, bearing or drive‑train resistance.
Triggered when conveyor speed falls to 0.6 m/s or below. Possible causes include mechanical jam, excessive belt resistance, drive‑train malfunction, motor or transmission problems.

Controller stops conveyor after sustained excessive‑load condition. Expected behavior: controller state STOPPED, motor current zero, speed zero, vibration at idle. Possible underlying causes: mechanical obstruction, excessive loading, bearing or drive‑train resistance.
On 2026-01-11, drive protection test confirmed overload shutdown function responded as expected.
On 2026-01-06, belt tension was adjusted and conveyor passed operational test.
On 2025-12-19, routine inspection reported motor current and vibration within expected ranges.

alternative_explanations: Excessive material load could have increased motor torque, raising current and reducing speed.
Bearing or drive‑train resistance (e.g., worn bearings) might have caused similar current and speed symptoms.
A transient temperature sensor fault could have mis‑reported motor temperature, but temperature remained within plausible range.
missing_evidence: Physical inspection report of the conveyor belt and rollers at the time of the event.
Load sensor data or material feed rate measurements preceding the shutdown.
Detailed vibration frequency spectrum to differentiate jam from bearing wear.
Motor torque or power measurement logs.
recommended_checks: Visually inspect conveyor for any mechanical obstruction or jammed material.
Verify belt tension and alignment; re‑adjust if out of spec.
Examine motor bearings and drive‑train for wear or resistance.
Review load/feed rate logs to assess whether an overload condition occurred.
Confirm calibration of motor current and speed sensors before restarting.

note: Structured evidence checks passed. Narrative and causal claims are not fully verified.
